Expurgate

EK-spur-gayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To expurgate is to remove offensive or objectionable material from something.

The museum agreed to expurgate the exhibit label after several visitors complained about its language.

Worked Example

Early American editions of the play were often expurgated before being taught in schools.

Editors weren't just editing for length -- they were specifically cutting the parts they considered offensive, which is exactly expurgate.

How Expurgate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

censor

censor: remove unacceptable parts of a text or work

bowdlerize

bowdlerize: remove material considered improper from a text

Antonyms

uncensored

uncensored: left complete, with nothing removed

How Strong Is It? — edit → expurgate → suppress

edit vs. expurgate

edit vs. expurgate: Editing simply revises a text for clarity or length; expurgating it specifically removes offensive content.

suppress vs. expurgate

suppress vs. expurgate: Expurgating removes specific offensive passages from a work; suppressing blocks the entire work from being seen at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ex-

prefix — ex-: out (Latin)

root — purg

root — purg: to cleanse (Latin (purgare))

suffix — -ate

suffix — -ate: to make or perform an action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Expurgate comes from Latin ex- ('out') + purgare ('to cleanse') + -ate -- literally 'to cleanse out.'

Use the root in a new word: purge

Use the root in a new word: purge: The same purgare root gives us purge, 'to rid something of unwanted parts,' and purgatory.
